pages.title: Xenoplasm
pages.text: Life fluid from another dimension. It does not use DNA, and its chemistry is foreign. It is warm, iridescent and moves on its own. Its molecules are built on a backbone no terrestrial cell would recognise, and their handedness alternates in ways that should be unstable. Somehow it thrives on that instability.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobiology studies life without DNA. In the Bioreactor, I combined a Xenogenome Sample with foam substrate and nutrient broth, and the culture grew as no Earth life could.
